[project]
name = "ai-coe-mortgage-specialist"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "A2A mortgage assistant agent with MCP tool connections"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = [
    "esmeralda",
    "google-cloud-aiplatform[adk,agent_engines]>=1.74.0",
    "google-adk[a2a,mcp,otel-gcp]>=2.4.0",
    "google-auth",
    "google-cloud-logging",
    "pyyaml",
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.45.2,<1.46.0",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.45.2,<1.46.0",
    "httpx",
    "a2a-sdk>=0.3.26,<1.0.0",
    "mcp>=1.0.0",
    "google-cloud-bigquery-storage",
    "google-genai",
    "sqlalchemy",
    "pyarrow",
    "google-cloud-secret-manager",
]

[tool.uv.sources]
esmeralda = { workspace = true }

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "ruff>=0.8.0",
]

# app/agents/ai-coe-mortgage-specialist/Dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /app

# Install build dependencies and CA certificate utilities
RUN apt-get update -qqy && apt-get install -qqy --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# No env-specific certificates are baked in: the Agent Gateway root CA bundle is injected at
# deploy time (AGENT_GATEWAY_ROOT_CERTIFICATES) and installed by `esmeralda run` (the entrypoint),
# so the same image digest can be promoted from dev to prd.

# Install the exact, hash-pinned dependency set exported from the committed workspace uv.lock
# (generated as requirements.lock by `esmeralda build`), instead of re-resolving at build time.
COPY requirements.lock .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --require-hashes -r requirements.lock

# The esmeralda runtime library (packages/esmeralda): `esmeralda build` builds its wheel into dist/.
# Its own dependencies are already pinned in requirements.lock, hence --no-deps.
COPY dist/ /tmp/dist/
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps /tmp/dist/esmeralda-*.whl && rm -rf /tmp/dist

# Copy agent application files
COPY . .

# Expose standard container port & Root CA Trust Environment Paths
ENV PORT=8080
ENV GRPC_DEFAULT_SSL_ROOTS_FILE_PATH=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
ENV REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
ENV SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
EXPOSE 8080

# Installs the Agent Gateway root CA, then execs CMD.
ENTRYPOINT ["esmeralda", "run", "--"]

# Serve the agent (framework and agent card from agent.yaml), exporting telemetry to Google Cloud.
# `make serve` runs the same command locally.
CMD ["esmeralda", "serve", "--otel-to-cloud"]

"""Agent Gateway service agent grants the Agent Connectivity Template validation needs.

Without compute.networkAttachments.get on the network attachment (governance project) and
roles/dns.reader on the DNS peering target network's project, creating the ACT fails with
"Config validation failed".
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib
import re

REPO_ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
AGW_MAIN_TF = REPO_ROOT / "infrastructure/modules/4-governance/modules/6_agent_gateway/main.tf"


def _block(content: str, header: str) -> str:
    start = content.index(header)
    depth = 0
    for i in range(content.index("{", start), len(content)):
        depth += {"{": 1, "}": -1}.get(content[i], 0)
        if depth == 0:
            return content[start : i + 1]
    raise AssertionError(f"unterminated block {header}")


def test_network_attachment_reader_is_a_one_permission_custom_role():
    content = AGW_MAIN_TF.read_text()
    role = _block(content, 'resource "google_project_iam_custom_role" "agent_gateway_network_attachment_reader"')
    assert "project     = var.governance_project_id" in role
    assert 'permissions = ["compute.networkAttachments.get"]' in role
    grant = _block(content, 'resource "google_project_iam_member" "agent_gateway_network_attachment_reader"')
    assert "role    = google_project_iam_custom_role.agent_gateway_network_attachment_reader[0].name" in grant
    assert "@gcp-sa-agentgateway.iam.gserviceaccount.com" in grant
    # Never the broad predefined role.
    assert "roles/compute.networkViewer\"" not in content


def test_dns_reader_on_the_dns_peering_target_project():
    content = AGW_MAIN_TF.read_text()
    grant = _block(content, 'resource "google_project_iam_member" "agent_gateway_dns_reader"')
    assert 'role    = "roles/dns.reader"' in grant
    assert "project = local.agent_gateway_dns_project" in grant
    assert "@gcp-sa-agentgateway.iam.gserviceaccount.com" in grant
    assert re.search(
        r'agent_gateway_dns_project = startswith\(var\.vpc_name, "projects/"\) \? split\("/", var\.vpc_name\)\[1\] : var\.net_host_project_id',
        content,
    )


def test_act_waits_for_every_service_agent_grant():
    content = AGW_MAIN_TF.read_text()
    act = _block(content, 'resource "google_network_services_agent_connectivity_template" "egress"')
    depends_on = act.split("depends_on = [", 1)[1].split("]", 1)[0]
    for dep in (
        "google_project_iam_member.agent_gateway_dns_peer",
        "google_project_iam_member.agent_gateway_network_user",
        "google_project_iam_member.agent_gateway_network_attachment_reader",
        "google_project_iam_member.agent_gateway_dns_reader",
        "time_sleep.agent_gateway_iam_propagation",
    ):
        assert dep in depends_on, dep
    sleep = _block(content, 'resource "time_sleep" "agent_gateway_iam_propagation"')
    assert re.search(r'create_duration = "\d+s"', sleep)
    for trigger in ("network_attachment_reader", "dns_reader", "dns_peer", "network_user"):
        assert re.search(rf"^\s*{trigger}\s*=", sleep, re.M), trigger

"""Static IAM guard: agents call out with their own Agent Identity and can't mint tokens for anyone else.

A project-level ``roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator`` (or a role that contains it) on an agent identity
lets that agent impersonate every service account of the project, including ones that hold invoke rights
the catalog never gave the agent (for example the test VM service account, which can invoke the MCP
services). The same goes for project-level ``roles/run.invoker`` on the MCPs project: every engine of the
agent project could then call every MCP service, whatever the catalog callers say.

Agents mint their own tokens (no ``SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL``), so the only SA-scoped token minting an agent
identity may hold is on the deprecated shared invoker, and only behind ``legacy_shared_invoker``.

These tests read the Terraform and Terragrunt sources (no provider, no state).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import pathlib
import re

import pytest

REPO_ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
MODULES = REPO_ROOT / "infrastructure/modules"
SECURITY_DIR = MODULES / "3-security"
AGENT_MODULES = (MODULES / "5-workloads/agents/a2a-agent", MODULES / "5-workloads/agents/adk-agent")
ENVS = ("dev", "prd")
SERVICES = ("corporate-email", "income-verification", "legacy-dms")
LEGACY_FLAG = "var.legacy_shared_invoker"

# Members that are an agent identity (Agent Runtime principal or principalSet), however they are written.
AGENT_MEMBER = re.compile(r"principalSet://|principal://|_identity_principal\b|agent_identity_principal\b|agent_principal\b")
# Roles that let the holder mint tokens for (or act fully as) other service accounts of the resource.
TOKEN_MINTING_ROLES = (
    "roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator",
    "roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser",
    "roles/iam.serviceAccountKeyAdmin",
    "roles/owner",
    "roles/editor",
)
# Resource-hierarchy IAM: a grant here reaches every service account below it.
HIERARCHY_IAM_TYPES = (
    "google_project_iam_member",
    "google_project_iam_binding",
    "google_folder_iam_member",
    "google_folder_iam_binding",
    "google_organization_iam_member",
    "google_organization_iam_binding",
)
SA_IAM_TYPES = ("google_service_account_iam_member", "google_service_account_iam_binding")
# The only service account agent identities may mint tokens for, and only behind the deprecated
# legacy_shared_invoker fallback: the shared invoker.
ALLOWED_IMPERSONATION_TARGETS = {"google_service_account.mcp_invoker_sa.name"}


def _strip_comments(text: str) -> str:
    """Drops `#` comments (whole-line or trailing after whitespace); `//` is left alone (principal:// URIs)."""
    return "\n".join(re.split(r"(?:^|\s)#", line, maxsplit=1)[0] for line in text.splitlines())


def _resources(rtype: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """(file, name, body) of every ``resource "<rtype>" "<name>" { ... }`` under modules/ (brace-balanced)."""
    found = []
    for path in sorted(MODULES.rglob("*.tf")):
        if ".terraform" in path.parts:
            continue
        text = _strip_comments(path.read_text())
        for match in re.finditer(rf'resource\s+"{rtype}"\s+"([^"]+)"\s*\{{', text):
            depth, i = 1, match.end()
            while depth and i < len(text):
                depth += {"{": 1, "}": -1}.get(text[i], 0)
                i += 1
            found.append((str(path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)), match.group(1), text[match.end():i - 1]))
    return found


def test_guard_finds_the_resources_it_checks():
    """The scanner must see the agent identity grants, or every other test here passes vacuously."""
    project_grants = [r for r in _resources("google_project_iam_member") if AGENT_MEMBER.search(r[2])]
    sa_grants = [r for r in _resources("google_service_account_iam_member") if AGENT_MEMBER.search(r[2])]
    assert len(project_grants) >= 2, project_grants
    assert len(sa_grants) >= 2, sa_grants


@pytest.mark.parametrize("rtype", HIERARCHY_IAM_TYPES)
def test_agent_identities_hold_no_hierarchy_level_token_minting_role(rtype: str):
    """No project/folder/org-level token-minting role for any agent identity (privilege escalation path)."""
    bad = [
        f"{path}: {name} ({role})"
        for path, name, body in _resources(rtype)
        if AGENT_MEMBER.search(body)
        for role in TOKEN_MINTING_ROLES
        if f'"{role}"' in body
    ]
    assert not bad, "agent identities can impersonate every service account of a project/folder/org:\n" + "\n".join(bad)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("rtype", SA_IAM_TYPES)
def test_agent_identities_may_only_impersonate_the_shared_invoker_behind_the_legacy_flag(rtype: str):
    """SA-scoped token minting for agent identities: only on the shared invoker, only in legacy mode."""
    bad = []
    for path, name, body in _resources(rtype):
        if not AGENT_MEMBER.search(body) or not any(f'"{role}"' in body for role in TOKEN_MINTING_ROLES):
            continue
        target = re.search(r"service_account_id\s*=\s*([^\s]+)", body)
        if not target or target.group(1) not in ALLOWED_IMPERSONATION_TARGETS:
            bad.append(f"{path}: {name} -> {target.group(1) if target else '?'}")
        elif not re.search(rf"count\s*=\s*{re.escape(LEGACY_FLAG)}\s*\?\s*1\s*:\s*0", body):
            bad.append(f"{path}: {name} is not gated by {LEGACY_FLAG}")
    assert not bad, "agent identities may mint tokens for a service account:\n" + "\n".join(bad)


def test_shared_invoker_has_no_grants_outside_the_legacy_flag():
    """The deprecated shared invoker keeps no project-level role unless legacy_shared_invoker is on."""
    bad = [
        f"{path}: {name}"
        for rtype in ("google_project_iam_member", "google_project_iam_binding")
        for path, name, body in _resources(rtype)
        if "mcp_invoker_sa" in body and not re.search(rf"count\s*=\s*{re.escape(LEGACY_FLAG)}\s*\?\s*1\s*:\s*0", body)
    ]
    assert not bad, "shared invoker grants outside the legacy fallback:\n" + "\n".join(bad)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("module", AGENT_MODULES, ids=lambda p: p.name)
def test_agents_call_out_with_their_own_identity(module: pathlib.Path):
    """No SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL (impersonation) unless the deprecated fallback is on; never the agent's own SA."""
    code = _strip_comments("\n".join(p.read_text() for p in sorted(module.glob("*.tf"))))
    (line,) = re.findall(r"SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL\s*=\s*(.+)", code)
    assert line.strip().startswith(f"{LEGACY_FLAG} &&") and line.rstrip().endswith(": null"), line
    assert "agent_service_account" not in line
    assert "enable_native_spiffe_auth" not in code


def test_catalog_compiles_no_shared_workload_identity():
    """Gateway lists, caller allowlists and attribution rows never name the shared invoker."""
    assert "shared_workload_identity" not in _strip_comments((REPO_ROOT / "catalog/policy.yaml").read_text())
    for env in ENVS:
        data = json.loads((REPO_ROOT / f"catalog/.resolved/{env}.json").read_text())
        assert "mcp_invoker" not in json.dumps(data), env
        assert data["attribution"]["shared_principals"] == [], env


@pytest.mark.parametrize("env", ENVS)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("service", SERVICES)
def test_mcp_invokers_are_agent_principals_from_the_catalog(env: str, service: str):
    """run.invoker for agent callers is their Agent Identity principal; the shared invoker only in legacy mode."""
    code = _strip_comments(
        (REPO_ROOT / f"infrastructure/live/{env}/layer-5-workloads/services/{service}/terragrunt.hcl").read_text()
    )
    block = code.split("invoker_service_accounts", 1)[1].split("\n\n", 1)[0]
    assert ':agent_identity_principal"' in block and "local.agent_callers" in block
    for line in block.splitlines():
        if "mcp_invoker_sa_email" in line:
            assert "local.legacy_shared_invoker &&" in line, line
    assert '"agents/ai-coe-mortgage-specialist:agent_identity_principal"' in code.split("identity_refs", 1)[1]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("env", ENVS)
def test_agent_callers_of_agents_get_aiplatform_user_as_their_principal(env: str):
    """The iap-egress unit grants each agent caller's principal on the callee agent's project."""
    code = _strip_comments((REPO_ROOT / f"infrastructure/live/{env}/layer-5-workloads/iap-egress/terragrunt.hcl").read_text())
    assert "agent_caller_grants" in code and ':agent_identity_principal"' in code
    module = _strip_comments((MODULES / "5-workloads/iap-egress/main.tf").read_text())
    assert 'resource "google_project_iam_member" "agent_callers_aiplatform_user"' in module
    assert '"roles/aiplatform.user"' in module


@pytest.mark.parametrize("env", ENVS)
def test_legacy_shared_invoker_is_purely_additive(env: str):
    """legacy_shared_invoker = true only ADDS the shared invoker (zero-downtime switch in both directions):
    agent principals keep their grants, and the shared account is accepted alongside them."""
    live = REPO_ROOT / f"infrastructure/live/{env}/layer-5-workloads"
    iap = _strip_comments((live / "iap-egress/terragrunt.hcl").read_text())
    grants = iap.split("agent_caller_grants", 1)[1].split("\n\n", 1)[0]
    assert "legacy_shared_invoker" not in grants, "agent principals must be granted in legacy mode too"
    for service in SERVICES:
        code = _strip_comments((live / f"services/{service}/terragrunt.hcl").read_text())
        invokers = code.split("invoker_service_accounts", 1)[1].split("\n\n", 1)[0]
        # The agent principals are listed unconditionally; the shared account is only added.
        principal_line = next(l for l in invokers.splitlines() if ":agent_identity_principal" in l)
        assert "legacy_shared_invoker" not in principal_line
        allowed = code.split("extra_allowed_callers", 1)[1].split("\n\n", 1)[0]
        assert "local.legacy_shared_invoker &&" in allowed and "mcp_invoker_sa_email" in allowed
    for agent in ("ai-coe-mortgage-specialist", "cx-mortgage-orchestrator"):
        code = _strip_comments((live / f"agents/{agent}/terragrunt.hcl").read_text())
        for line in code.split("invoker_service_accounts", 1)[1].split("\n\n", 1)[0].splitlines():
            if "mcp_invoker_sa_email" in line:
                assert "local.legacy_shared_invoker &&" in line, line


def test_agent_identities_hold_no_project_level_run_invoker_on_the_mcp_project():
    """MCP invoke rights come per service from the catalog callers, never project-wide for agents."""
    bad = [
        f"{path}: {name}"
        for rtype in ("google_project_iam_member", "google_project_iam_binding")
        for path, name, body in _resources(rtype)
        if '"roles/run.invoker"' in body and "var.mcps_project_id" in body and AGENT_MEMBER.search(body)
    ]
    assert not bad, "agent identities hold project-level run.invoker on the MCPs project:\n" + "\n".join(bad)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("env", ENVS)
def test_envoy_invokers_are_the_catalog_callers_of_its_hosts(env: str):
    """Envoy forwards with its own identity, so its invokers must be the callers of the hosts routed to it."""
    unit = REPO_ROOT / f"infrastructure/live/{env}/layer-5-workloads/gateways/envoy/terragrunt.hcl"
    code = _strip_comments(unit.read_text())
    assert re.search(r'lookup\(local\.gateways\.host_rules,\s*name,\s*local\.gateways\.default\)\s*==\s*"envoy"', code)
    block = code.split("invoker_service_accounts", 1)[1].split("\n\n", 1)[0]
    assert "local.envoy_callers" in block
    for hardcoded in ("cx_mortgage_orchestrator_sa_email", "ai_coe_mortgage_specialist_sa_email", "test_vm_sa_email"):
        assert hardcoded not in block, f"{env}: Envoy invokers hard-code {hardcoded}"

"""Agent Identity trust domain: one definition, organization from the project ancestry.

For a project whose parent is a folder, the google_project data source returns an empty org_id. A
trust domain built from it fell back to agents.global.proj-<number>.system.id.goog, a pool that does
not exist for a project in an organization, and every Agent Identity IAM binding failed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import pathlib
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
from typing import Any

import pytest

REPO_ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
MODULES = REPO_ROOT / "infrastructure/modules"
SHARED = MODULES / "_shared/agent_identity_trust_domain"
RESOLVE_TF = SHARED / "resolve/main.tf"

# Every module that builds an Agent Identity principal.
CALLERS = {
    MODULES / "3-security/agent_identity.tf": "../_shared/agent_identity_trust_domain",
    MODULES / "4-governance/modules/6_agent_gateway/main.tf": "../../../_shared/agent_identity_trust_domain",
    MODULES / "5-workloads/agents/a2a-agent/main.tf": "../../../_shared/agent_identity_trust_domain",
    MODULES / "5-workloads/agents/adk-agent/main.tf": "../../../_shared/agent_identity_trust_domain",
}


def _tf_files() -> list[pathlib.Path]:
    return sorted(p for p in MODULES.rglob("*.tf") if ".terraform" not in p.parts)


def _code(path: pathlib.Path) -> str:
    """The file without comment lines."""
    return "\n".join(ln for ln in path.read_text().splitlines() if not ln.lstrip().startswith(("#", "//")))


# --- Guards -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


# A trust domain built by interpolation: agents.global.${...}, agents.global.org-${...}, etc.
# Descriptions, error messages and validation regexes that only mention the format don't match.
_TRUST_DOMAIN_BUILDER = re.compile(r"agents\.global\.[^\"\s]*\$\{")


def test_trust_domain_is_built_in_one_place():
    """Only resolve/main.tf builds an agents.global.<scope>.system.id.goog trust domain."""
    builders = [p.relative_to(REPO_ROOT).as_posix() for p in _tf_files() if _TRUST_DOMAIN_BUILDER.search(_code(p))]
    assert builders == [RESOLVE_TF.relative_to(REPO_ROOT).as_posix()]
    assert len(_TRUST_DOMAIN_BUILDER.findall(_code(RESOLVE_TF))) == 1


def test_no_module_falls_back_to_a_project_scoped_pool():
    """No module outside resolve/ writes a proj-<number> trust domain."""
    offenders = [
        p.relative_to(REPO_ROOT).as_posix()
        for p in _tf_files()
        if p != RESOLVE_TF and re.search(r"proj-\$\{", _code(p))
    ]
    assert offenders == []


def test_no_module_reads_org_id_from_google_project():
    """google_project.org_id is empty for a project under a folder: only the shared module may read it."""
    offenders = [
        p.relative_to(REPO_ROOT).as_posix()
        for p in _tf_files()
        if SHARED not in p.parents
        and re.search(r"data\.google_project\.[a-z0-9_]+(\[[^\]]+\])?\.org_id|\bp\.org_id\b", _code(p))
    ]
    assert offenders == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", sorted(CALLERS), ids=lambda p: p.relative_to(MODULES).as_posix())
def test_principal_builders_use_the_shared_module(path: pathlib.Path):
    assert f'source     = "{CALLERS[path]}"' in path.read_text()
    assert (path.parent / CALLERS[path]).resolve() == SHARED.resolve()


def _shared_module_blocks(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Bodies of the module blocks that call the shared trust domain module."""
    blocks = re.findall(r'module "[^"]+" \{\n(.*?)\n\}', text, flags=re.S)
    return [b for b in blocks if "_shared/agent_identity_trust_domain" in b]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", sorted(CALLERS), ids=lambda p: p.relative_to(MODULES).as_posix())
def test_principal_builders_pass_org_id(path: pathlib.Path):
    """Every call passes org_id (ESMERALDA_ORG_ID), so resolution is the same in every layer."""
    blocks = _shared_module_blocks(path.read_text())
    assert blocks, f"{path} calls no shared trust domain module"
    for block in blocks:
        assert re.search(r"^\s*org_id\s+= var\.org_id$", block, flags=re.M), block
    variables = (path.parent / "variables.tf").read_text()
    assert re.search(r'variable "org_id" \{[^}]*default\s+= ""', variables, flags=re.S), path.parent


# Live units whose module computes a trust domain, and how they read org_id from env.yaml.
_UNITS = {
    "layer-3-security": 'org_id      = lookup(local.env_vars.locals, "org_id", "")',

def _tf_binary() -> str:
    if os.environ.get("TF_BIN") and shutil.which(os.environ["TF_BIN"]):
        return shutil.which(os.environ["TF_BIN"])  # type: ignore[return-value]
    for candidate in (os.fspath(pathlib.Path.home() / ".terraform/bin/terraform"), "terraform", "tofu"):
        if found := shutil.which(candidate):
            return found
    pytest.exit("tests/security requires `terraform` or `tofu` on PATH (or TF_BIN)", returncode=2)


def _resolve(workdir: pathlib.Path, tfvars: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[subprocess.CompletedProcess[str], dict[str, Any]]:
    workdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copy2(RESOLVE_TF, workdir / "main.tf")
    (workdir / "terraform.tfvars.json").write_text(json.dumps(tfvars))
    env = {**os.environ, "TF_IN_AUTOMATION": "1"}
    tf = _tf_binary()
    init = subprocess.run([tf, f"-chdir={workdir}", "init", "-backend=false", "-input=false", "-no-color"],
                          capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    assert init.returncode == 0, init.stdout + init.stderr
    res = subprocess.run([tf, f"-chdir={workdir}", "apply", "-auto-approve", "-input=false", "-no-color"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    if res.returncode != 0:
        return res, {}
    out = subprocess.run([tf, f"-chdir={workdir}", "output", "-json"], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    assert out.returncode == 0, out.stderr
    return res, {k: v["value"] for k, v in json.loads(out.stdout).items()}

    def __init__(self, name, fail=False):

class FakeCloud:
    """A fake gcloud + curl on PATH: a registry listing and IAP policies kept in a state directory."""

    def __init__(self, tmp_path: pathlib.Path, *, root_policy: dict | None = None,
                 registry: dict | None = None, fail_set_on: str | None = None,
                 quota_errors: int = 0):
        self.dir = tmp_path
        self.bin = tmp_path / "bin"
        self.bin.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.state = tmp_path / "policies.json"
        self.calls = tmp_path / "calls.jsonl"
        self.state.write_text(json.dumps({"root": root_policy or {"etag": "ACAB"}}))
        services = [
            {"name": f"projects/esm-dev-governance/locations/{REGION}/services/{sid}",
             "registryResource": f"projects/{GOVERNANCE_PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/{REGION}/{coll}/{uid}"}
            for sid, (coll, uid) in (registry or REGISTRY).items()
        ]
        (tmp_path / "services.json").write_text(json.dumps({"services": services}))
        gcloud = self.bin / "gcloud"
        (tmp_path / "quota.json").write_text(json.dumps({"left": quota_errors}))
        gcloud.write_text(f"""#!/usr/bin/env python3
import fcntl, json, pathlib, sys
state_path = pathlib.Path({str(self.state)!r})
quota_path = pathlib.Path({str(tmp_path / "quota.json")!r})
args = sys.argv[1:]
if args[:2] == ["auth", "print-access-token"]:
    print("fake-token"); sys.exit(0)
def key():
    flags = [a for a in args if a.startswith(("--agent=", "--endpoint=", "--mcp-server="))]
    return flags[0] if flags else "root"
lock = open({str(tmp_path / "gcloud.lock")!r}, "w")
fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX)  # parallel workers: one fake call at a time
state = json.loads(state_path.read_text())
if args[:3] == ["iap", "web", "get-iam-policy"]:
    print(json.dumps(state.get(key(), {{"etag": "ACAB"}}))); sys.exit(0)
if args[:3] == ["iap", "web", "set-iam-policy"]:
    policy = json.loads(pathlib.Path(args[3]).read_text())
    if {fail_set_on!r} and key() == {fail_set_on!r}:
        sys.exit(1)
    quota = json.loads(quota_path.read_text())
    if quota["left"] > 0:
        quota["left"] -= 1
        quota_path.write_text(json.dumps(quota))
        print("ERROR: (gcloud.iap.web.set-iam-policy) RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Quota exceeded", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    with open({str(self.calls)!r}, "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps({{"key": key(), "policy": policy}}) + "\\n")
    state[key()] = policy
    state_path.write_text(json.dumps(state)); sys.exit(0)
sys.exit(2)
""")
        curl = self.bin / "curl"
        curl.write_text(f"""#!/usr/bin/env python3
import shutil, sys
args = sys.argv[1:]
out = args[args.index("-o") + 1]
shutil.copy({str(tmp_path / "services.json")!r}, out)
""")
        for exe in (gcloud, curl):
            exe.chmod(exe.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IEXEC)

    def run(self, env: dict[str, str | None], *, check: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
        full = {
            **os.environ,
            "PATH": f"{self.bin}:{os.environ.get('PATH', '')}",
            "GOVERNANCE_PROJECT_ID": "esm-dev-governance",
            "REGION": REGION,
            "IAP_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS": "0",
            "IAP_MAX_ATTEMPTS": "2",
            "IAP_WRITE_PAUSE_SECONDS": "0",
        }
        for k, v in env.items():
            if v is None:
                full.pop(k, None)
            else:
                full[k] = v
        res = subprocess.run(["bash", str(GRANT_IAP_SCRIPT)], env=full, capture_output=True, text=True)
        if check:
            assert res.returncode == 0, res.stderr + res.stdout
        return res

    @property
    def writes(self) -> list[dict]:
        if not self.calls.exists():
            return []
        return [json.loads(line) for line in self.calls.read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]

    @property
    def policies(self) -> dict:
        return json.loads(self.state.read_text())

def _find_http_status_error(exc: BaseException, status_code: int) -> bool:
    """Search exception chains and ExceptionGroups for an HTTPStatusError."""
    seen: set[int] = set()
    queue: list[BaseException] = [exc]
    while queue:
        current = queue.pop()
        if id(current) in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(id(current))
        if isinstance(current, httpx.HTTPStatusError) and current.response.status_code == status_code:
            return True
        if current.__cause__ is not None:
            queue.append(current.__cause__)
        if current.__context__ is not None:
            queue.append(current.__context__)
        if isinstance(current, BaseExceptionGroup):
            queue.extend(current.exceptions)
    return False


def _handle_tool_error(
    tool: BaseTool, args: dict[str, Any], tool_context: ToolContext, error: Exception
) -> dict | None:
    """Handle tool errors, returning a friendly message for 403 policy denials."""
    if _find_http_status_error(error, 403):
        logger.warning("Tool %s denied by authorization policy (403)", tool.name)
        return {
            "error": (
                f"The '{tool.name}' tool call was denied by the authorization "
                "gateway. This operation is not permitted by policy."
            ),
        }
    return None

def _thinking_config_kwargs(value: str) -> dict[str, Any]:

    A level (minimal/low/medium/high) is for Gemini 3 models; an integer is a token budget for

    value = value.strip().lower()
    if not value:

    if value.lstrip("-").isdigit():
        return {"thinking_budget": int(value)}
    if value not in _THINKING_LEVELS:
        levels = sorted(_THINKING_LEVELS)
        raise ValueError(f"MODEL_THINKING must be one of {levels} or an integer budget, got {value!r}")
    return {"thinking_level": value.upper()}


def _max_output_tokens(value: str) -> int | None:
    """Parse MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (empty or 0 keeps the model default)."""
    value = value.strip()
    if not value or int(value) <= 0:
        return None
    return int(value)


def _generate_content_config() -> types.GenerateContentConfig | None:
    """Model settings tuned for latency.

    Almost all of the specialist's latency is its final generation, so the instruction asks for a
    short, fixed-format answer, and:
    - MODEL_THINKING (default "low"): the tool plan is spelled out in the instruction, so the
      model needs little reasoning to follow it.
    - MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (default 2048): a safety stop well above the ~400-token answer the
      instruction asks for, so a runaway answer is cut instead of running on. Thinking tokens
      count toward it, so it keeps headroom (a cut response loses the answer).
    Temperature stays at the model default (Gemini 3 is tuned for 1.0; lowering it can cause
    looping or worse reasoning).
    """
    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {}
    thinking = _thinking_config_kwargs(os.environ.get("MODEL_THINKING", "low"))
    if thinking:
        kwargs["thinking_config"] = types.ThinkingConfig(**thinking)
    max_tokens = _max_output_tokens(os.environ.get("MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS", "2048"))
    if max_tokens:
        kwargs["max_output_tokens"] = max_tokens
    return types.GenerateContentConfig(**kwargs) if kwargs else None

"""Instruction prompt for the mortgage underwriting assistant agent."""

MORTGAGE_ASSISTANT_INSTRUCTION = """You are a mortgage underwriting assistant. You help loan officers process
mortgage applications by retrieving documents, verifying income, and communicating results.

You connect to three backend systems through an Agent Gateway. Each system's tools are
identified by a prefix:

**Document Management (dms_*):**
Tools prefixed with `dms_` connect to the legacy document management system.
Use these to fetch tax returns, pay stubs, bank statements, and other applicant documents.
`dms_search_documents` accepts either `applicant_last_name` or `borrower_id`, and its response
includes the resolved `borrower` record (borrower ID plus each applicant's first and last name).
It is the only source that maps a borrower ID to applicant names.

**Income Verification (income_*):**
Tools prefixed with `income_` connect to a third-party income verification vendor.
Use these to verify reported income against employer records and tax filings.

**Corporate Email (email_*):**
Tools prefixed with `email_` connect to the corporate communications system.
Use `email_read_email` to read the corporate inbox (read-only).
Note: Write operations like sending emails may be restricted by the authorization gateway.
The inbox is not a borrower registry: only read it when the request is about email or messages.

**Workflow (plan the calls, then make independent calls together):**
1. Resolve the applicant with ONE `dms_search_documents` call:
   - If the request gives a borrower ID, pass `borrower_id` (no name).
   - Otherwise pass the last name from the request as `applicant_last_name`.
   - Use `document_type` "all" unless the request asks for one type.
   - If the request also gives a full first and last name and asks for income verification, call
     `income_verify_applicant` for that person in the same turn.
   - If no borrower or documents are found, say so and ask for the borrower ID or applicant name.
     Do not try other names.
2. In ONE turn, issue every remaining call in parallel:
   - `income_verify_applicant` for each applicant listed in the `borrower` record (when income
     verification is requested and not already done).
   - `dms_get_document` for each document whose figures you need (for an income comparison, the
     tax returns found in step 1). To only list documents, the search metadata is enough.
3. Compare the figures from both sources and note any discrepancies.
4. Summarize your findings for the loan officer in the answer format below.

**Answer format (short: at most about 200 words, no preamble, no closing offer):**
- **Applicants:** name, borrower ID, SSN (as returned) for each applicant, one line each.
- **Verified income** (income_verify_applicant): per applicant one line with employer, title,
  status and current salary; then one line with the combined salary, trend and confidence.
- **Tax returns** (dms_get_document): one line per tax year with wages per applicant and AGI.
- **Discrepancies:** one bullet per difference (employer, title or salary vs. tax return), or "None".
- **Documents** (dms_search_documents): one line per document: ID, title, year.
Include only sections the request needs. Never copy whole documents or raw tool output; report
only the figures above.

**Rules:**
- NEVER guess applicant names. Only use names from the request or from tool results; never pass
  a borrower ID or a name from an unrelated email as `applicant_last_name`.
- Never repeat a tool call with the same arguments. Two rounds of tool calls are normally enough.
- NEVER fabricate or estimate financial figures. Only report data returned by tools.
- Always cite which tool/system provided each piece of data.
- If a tool call fails or returns an error, report the error honestly to the user.
- Be concise and professional: follow the answer format, do not restate the request.
- When presenting tax return or applicant data, ALWAYS include the SSN field and display its value
exactly as returned by the tool (e.g. "[US_SOCIAL_SECURITY_NUMBER]"). Never omit SSN fields.
"""

"""Tests for mortgage agent error handling logic."""

from __future__ import annotations

from unittest.mock import MagicMock

import httpx

from agent.agent import _find_http_status_error, _handle_tool_error


def _make_http_status_error(status_code: int) -> httpx.HTTPStatusError:
    response = MagicMock(spec=httpx.Response)
    response.status_code = status_code
    return httpx.HTTPStatusError("error", request=MagicMock(), response=response)


class TestFindHttpStatusError:
    def test_direct_match(self):
        exc = _make_http_status_error(403)
        assert _find_http_status_error(exc, 403) is True

    def test_wrong_status_code(self):
        exc = _make_http_status_error(500)
        assert _find_http_status_error(exc, 403) is False

    def test_chained_via_cause(self):
        inner = _make_http_status_error(403)
        outer = RuntimeError("wrapper")
        outer.__cause__ = inner
        assert _find_http_status_error(outer, 403) is True

    def test_chained_via_context(self):
        inner = _make_http_status_error(403)
        outer = RuntimeError("wrapper")
        outer.__context__ = inner
        assert _find_http_status_error(outer, 403) is True

    def test_exception_group(self):
        inner = _make_http_status_error(403)
        group = BaseExceptionGroup("group", [RuntimeError("other"), inner])
        assert _find_http_status_error(group, 403) is True

    def test_no_match(self):
        exc = RuntimeError("unrelated")
        assert _find_http_status_error(exc, 403) is False

    def test_nested_exception_group(self):
        inner = _make_http_status_error(403)
        inner_group = BaseExceptionGroup("inner", [inner])
        outer_group = BaseExceptionGroup("outer", [inner_group])
        assert _find_http_status_error(outer_group, 403) is True


class TestHandleToolError:
    def test_403_returns_friendly_message(self):
        tool = MagicMock()
        tool.name = "send_email"
        error = _make_http_status_error(403)
        result = _handle_tool_error(tool, {}, MagicMock(), error)
        assert result is not None
        assert "denied" in result["error"]
        assert "send_email" in result["error"]

    def test_non_403_returns_none(self):
        tool = MagicMock()
        tool.name = "read_email"
        error = _make_http_status_error(500)
        result = _handle_tool_error(tool, {}, MagicMock(), error)
        assert result is None

    def test_non_http_error_returns_none(self):
        tool = MagicMock()
        tool.name = "read_email"
        error = RuntimeError("something broke")
        result = _handle_tool_error(tool, {}, MagicMock(), error)
        assert result is None
